names: Sidónio Bernardino Cardoso da Silva Pais
summary: Sidónio Pais (1872–1918), an army officer and professor of mathematics who had been a minister and then Portugal's envoy in Berlin, overthrew the Democratic government in December 1917 and governed as head of a junta and then as a directly elected president, with the parties displaced and parliament reduced. His "New Republic" restored relations with the Church, courted Catholic and monarchist support, and drew on a personal popularity that the republic's parties had never had; it also arrested opponents and did not survive its author. He was shot dead at Rossio station in December 1918. Some historians read the episode as a first Portuguese experiment with charismatic authoritarian rule and a precedent later regimes drew on; others treat it as a personal government with no doctrine behind it. He is in the atlas as the republic's one attempt to be governed by one man before 1926.
